summary: Feed 'combined' to IDS is degraded: 13.8% duplicate packets and 40% one-way TCP sessions (80/200). IDS requires bidirectional, full-payload traffic and is missing return direction for stateful analysis.

findings.root_cause: Only one direction of 40% of TCP sessions reaches the IDS. Feed 'combined' likely aggregates SPAN/TAP sources with incomplete coverage or packet broker policy that splits directions across different tool ports / asymmetric routing where only one side is tapped, so return traffic is not aggregated to this IDS port.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs both directions for TCP handshake tracking, stream reassembly and bidirectional signature matching. With 40% one-way flows the IDS cannot establish state, misses payload in response, and fails to detect exploits, C2 and data exfiltration.

recommended_fix.why: Configure packet broker to aggregate both directions of each flow to the same IDS tool port using symmetric 5-tuple hashing and verify TAP/SPAN sources capture both Tx and Rx for all monitored links.

findings.root_cause: Feed 'combined' aggregates multiple overlapping SPAN/TAP sources without broker deduplication. The same packet ingressing on two monitored links is forwarded twice to the IDS, causing 401 of 2903 packets (13.8%) to be duplicates, above 5% threshold.
findings.impact_on_tool: Wastes IDS 1Gbps capacity and CPU on redundant 13.8% traffic, inflates flow counts, skews analytics and can cause false positives or mask rate-based detections while reducing headroom for real traffic.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet broker deduplication on the combined feed to drop identical packets seen within a short time window before delivery to the IDS, preserving capacity for unique traffic.
